page_title: Keelhaven — back up your Mac to storage you own

sources.entry: Keelhaven - Menu bar app that runs scheduled, encrypted restic backups to a local disk, S3, SFTP, or a REST server. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/shenxianpeng/keelhaven) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Keelhaven
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that encrypts folders on your Mac and backs them up on a schedule to storage you own, using the restic engine.
use_cases: Keep an encrypted offsite copy of important Mac folders
Back up folders to an S3 bucket or Backblaze B2
Back up to a NAS over SFTP
Schedule hourly, daily or weekly Mac backups
Restore individual files or snapshots from a past date
Complement Time Machine with a second copy
summary.what_it_does: Keelhaven is a menu bar app that encrypts chosen Mac folders and backs them up on an hourly, daily or weekly schedule to an external or network drive, an S3-compatible bucket, SFTP server or restic REST server. Each run stores only changed data as a deduplicated snapshot. Repository passwords are kept in the macOS Keychain. Restores go into a new folder by default, and selected files can be restored from a snapshot. Repositories are standard restic, so they can be restored with the restic CLI on Mac or Linux without Keelhaven. The app runs an integrity check on a schedule, weekly by default, and reports failed runs in the menu bar and by notification.
notable: Standard restic repositories, restorable without Keelhaven
Passwords held in macOS Keychain; no account, server or telemetry
Retention policies and upload-rate limits per plan
Open source under GPLv3; install via Homebrew cask or curl script
caveats: Public beta; builds are not yet notarised, so macOS shows a security warning on first launch and Full Disk Access must be re-granted after updates
Not on the Mac App Store because App Store sandboxing conflicts with the backup engine's needs
If the repository password is lost, the backup is unrecoverable by design
